standard.label: Standard
standard.summary: The common reading. A foil unlocks its family the way the community usually plays it, and gathering an item before its card is unlocked is allowed as long as you bank it.
caveats: You may gather and bank an item before its card is unlocked. You just cannot use it until then.

sources.label: Project brief - downward unlocks
osrscardexchange - Foil cards: what people say
sources.quote: vertical/downward unlocks, described as the leading consensus

extreme.label: Extreme
extreme.summary: The strict cardlocked-ironman reading. The same cards are unlocked, but you may not interact with a locked source at all - no gathering ahead of the unlock and no pre-banking.
caveats: Any interaction with a locked source is off the table. You cannot gather, mine, chop or catch a card you have not unlocked, even to bank it.

sources.label: Extreme defined from the osrscardexchange framing only
osrscardexchange - Foil cards: what people say

plain-foil.label: Plain foil
plain-foil.summary: A foil is just a shiny duplicate. It unlocks the card it shows and nothing more. A vocal minority position, shown here as a first-class answer rather than an error.
caveats: This is one of three community camps, not a settled rule. It is the most conservative reading available.

sources.label: osrscardexchange - Foil cards: what people say
sources.quote: a foil is just a foil

rules.explanation: A foil armour piece unlocks that piece and every tier of it below. {card} covers {count} cards down to {lowest}. The {excludedCount} tiers above stay locked.

sources.label: Project brief - downward unlocks
sources.quote: A foil armour piece unlocks that piece and all tiers of the same piece below it, not above. Rune full helm -> all full helms Rune and below.

rules.explanation: A foil weapon unlocks that weapon and every tier of it below. {card} covers {count} cards down to {lowest}. The {excludedCount} tiers above stay locked.

sources.label: Project brief - downward unlocks
sources.quote: Same for weapon types. Mithril platebody, Iron platelegs behave identically.

rules.explanation: A foil resource unlocks the verbs for that resource and everything below it. {card} covers {count} cards down to {lowest}. You get the actions, not what they produce.

sources.label: Project brief - downward unlocks
sources.quote: A foil resource unlocks the relevant verbs for that resource and all below it, but not the downstream product.

sources.label: Resource unlocks grant verbs, not downstream products

rules.explanation: An item with an unprocessed and a processed form unlocks both forms of {card} and nothing else. It does not descend any ladder the card also sits in.
caveats: Not everyone reads it this way. One community source treats a foil fish as unlocking every fish caught the same way. That reading is recorded here as input and not adopted - a pair is one item in two forms, so it stops a descent rather than starting one.

sources.label: State pairs unlock both states only, and beat downward unlocks
State-pair rule widened to cut gems and tanned hides

rules.explanation: TheSeahorsie's foil rules give this ladder explicitly: go down vertically in progression and unlock everything under. {card} covers {count} cards down to {lowest}. The {excludedCount} above stay locked.

rules.explanation: The elemental and catalytic rune ladder descends. {card} covers {count} cards down to {lowest}. The {excludedCount} above stay locked.

rules.explanation: Combination runes unlock other combination runes, following the downward unlock rule among themselves. {card} covers {count} cards down to {lowest}. The {excludedCount} above stay locked.
caveats: A combination rune is made from two elemental runes, so reading a foil one as unlocking those runes is a fair argument. It was considered and not adopted - this ladder stands separate from the elemental one.

sources.label: Combination runes form their own descending ladder
